chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) performed Tawaf upon his she-camel, Al-Adhba', and he would touch the corners with his staff and kiss the staff.'
ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet Muhammad perform Tawaf while riding his camel?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Prophet Muhammad’s (peace be upon him) flexibility in ritual practice, specifically demonstrating that using a staff (*mihsan*) to touch the corners of the Kaaba while riding is a valid form of *Istilam* (touching the corners). In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a primary evidence (*hujjah*) for the permissibility of using an object to perform ritual gestures when physical contact is不便 or necessary, such as during illness or while mounted. The act of kissing the staff further emphasizes the spiritual significance of the gesture itself, rather than the direct skin-to-skin contact with the stone.
